doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Audio examples: a coined phrase and 'Walk On with Hope'
summary: Over playback of his songs he explains an expression coined by an ex-wife and the audience laughter at a cliche-filled song.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I have a couple of little pieces of material that I wanted to—
I’m afraid I don’t know what that means.
Well yeah, it means to flirt outrageously with somebody. One of my wives, an ex-wife of mine made that up — that expression up.
And I thought it was very colorful. I have no idea what cakes she’s talking about. But it’s interesting, it’s a good turn of phrase.
Isn’t it. I like it. It’s interesting where inspiration comes from sometimes. This is one of my favorite things that is somewhat borrowing I guess.
Can you still hit those notes? I really love what you did with “Walk on, Walk on with Hope in Your Heart.”
Yeah a lot of people laugh, I love it when they laugh at that. I think it’s funny too.
